record.excerpt: A base order fires when 4h RSI(14) drops below 28 … Five averaging orders at fixed deviations (−2%, −5%, −9.5%, −16%, −25%) with 1.8× size scaling per rung. … Take Profit: 3% above average entry. … Stop Loss: None — ladder allocation is the structural risk cap. … Test Period: January 1, 2024 — June 29, 2026 (~30 months). … Net Profit: +3,078.29 USDT (+3.08%) … Percent Profitable: 70.97% (44 / 62) … Profit Factor: 4.028
record.notes: RSI<28 4h entry with DCA ladder and 3% TP, no stop; explicit test period and stats. Page shows Jun 30 without year; year inferred from test period ending Jun 29 2026.

spec.claim_summary: A 4-hour RSI(14) strategy enters when RSI drops below 28, layers five scaled averaging orders at fixed drawdowns, and targets 3% above average entry with no stop.
spec.untestable_reason: The strategy's edge and risk depend on five scaled averaging orders and TP from averaged entry, which the single-position schema cannot express.
assumptions: Asset is BTCUSDT: the claim text names no asset; the page context about BTC is not quoted and this is the most natural reading.
Timeframe is 4h from the claim's '4h RSI(14)'.
Direction is long: inferred from base order plus averaging down at negative deviations and TP above average entry with no short language.
'drops below 28' compiled as crosses_below 28 on bar closes with fill at next open per engine convention.

NOT EXPRESSIBLE: Five averaging orders at fixed deviations (-2%, -5%, -9.5%, -16%, -25%) with 1.8x size scaling per rung and ladder allocation as structural risk cap cannot be expressed; the engine tests one position at a time with no DCA/pyramiding or position sizing.

NOT EXPRESSIBLE: Take Profit 3% above average entry including ladder fills and sizing cannot be expressed; take_profit_pct=3 from initial entry is only a proxy and is a different exit level once any averaging order fills.
Claimed performance corresponds to the full ladder system, not to the single-position proxy.

issues.problem: Omits five averaging orders at -2%, -5%, -9.5%, -16%, -25% with 1.8x size scaling per rung. Spec tests single-position entry only, which changes position sizing, average entry and risk exposure.
Claim requires 3% above average entry including ladder fills and sizing; spec uses 3% from initial entry as proxy, which is a different exit level once any averaging order fills.
